body: Suresh, since you're already hitting 18 orders/day on your ₹149 Weekday Lunch Thali, let's scale this for Indiranagar offices. I've drafted a bulk package with volume pricing, a fixed order cut-off, and a single delivery window to keep your operations smooth. Should I send over the Google post and WhatsApp copy for you to share with office admins? Reply YES.
rationale: I used the 'proven demand' signal (18 orders/day) to validate the effort of creating a corporate package, making the merchant more likely to accept the ready-to-use marketing assets. [Merchant already asked ('Yes good idea, what would it look like') — no more qualifying; handed over a concrete plan built on our earlier proposal/their own numbers, one next step.]

body: Padma, let's lock in that kids yoga summer camp while interest is high. I've structured a 4-week program (3 classes/week, ages 7-12) at ₹2,499, including a seat cap to drive urgency. I have the Google post and WhatsApp copy ready to go. Reply YES and I'll send them for your approval.
rationale: I used the 'urgency' lever by highlighting the seat cap and the specific program structure to make the decision feel like a completed task for the busy merchant. [Merchant already asked ('Hi I want to add a kids yoga program — what should it look like?') — no more qualifying; handed over a concrete plan built on our earlier proposal/their own numbers, one next step.]

body: Hi Aditya, Karim's Salon here. We have your appointment scheduled for tomorrow and are keeping your chair ready. Reply YES to confirm, or let us know if you need to reschedule.
rationale: I used the 'keeping your chair ready' framing to create a sense of personal service and accountability, which encourages a quick confirmation from the customer. [Appointment reminder — reduces no-shows; one-tap confirm, reschedule path open.]

body: Hi Riya, Beauty Lounge by Renu here. Just a quick reminder for your appointment tomorrow. We are expecting a busy day, so please let us know if you're still coming. Reply YES to confirm.
rationale: I used the 'busy day' social proof signal to create a sense of urgency, encouraging the customer to confirm their slot so the merchant can manage their schedule effectively. [Appointment reminder — reduces no-shows; one-tap confirm, reschedule path open.]

body: Hi Ramesh, summer demand is shifting: ORS, sunscreen, and anti-fungal sales are up 40-45%, while cold/cough is down 60%. Move these essentials to your front counter to capture the trend. Should I draft a 'season essentials' Google post and WhatsApp message for your repeat customers to boost visibility? Reply YES.
rationale: I used the specific seasonal demand shift percentages to create urgency and leveraged the merchant's high repeat customer base (68%) as a compelling reason to engage them. [Seasonal demand shift with concrete % moves; shelf action + ready-made content offer.]

body: Dr. Meera, IDA Delhi is hosting a session on 2 May at 7pm covering CAD/CAM workflow ROI and the latest on Primescan 2 and Trios 5. It’s worth 2 CDE credits and is free for IDA members (₹500 for others). Should I reserve your seat and set a reminder for one hour before? Reply YES.
rationale: I used the 'professional development' signal to appeal to the merchant's clinical growth, framing the webinar as a high-value ROI discussion for their practice. [Continuing-education event with date + credits; effort externalised (I register/remind).]

body: Namaste Sharma ji, Apollo Health Plus Pharmacy se refill reminder: aapki 3 regular medicines (metformin, atorvastatin, telmisartan) 28 April ko khatam ho rahi hain. Senior Citizen 15% OFF ke saath hum same dose pack kar rahe hain, aur ₹499 se upar delivery free hai. Kya saved address par bhej dein? Reply CONFIRM.
rationale: I used the 'loss aversion' signal by highlighting the specific expiry date (28 April) to prompt immediate action, while maintaining the trustworthy tone and including the relevant senior citizen discount. [Chronic refill: exact molecules + run-out date; existing senior/delivery offers; addressed correctly when the chat goes via a family member; dosage-change safety valve.]

body: Hi Vivaan, Dr. Sameer here. Following your 1 Apr visit, JIDA (Oct 2026) research suggests that for patients with your history, a 3-month recall interval is more effective than 6 months for preventing caries recurrence. Shall we pre-book your next check-up for early July? Reply YES.
rationale: I used the JIDA research signal to provide a clinical, evidence-based reason for the follow-up, which shifts the tone from a generic reminder to a professional recommendation. [Refill-type trigger on a dentist (not a pharmacy): framed as a routine check-up follow-up instead of a medicine refill. Customer recall on behalf of merchant: real last-visit date, slots/offer only if they exist, 'due' claimed only when the interval supports it; language preference honoured.]

body: Dr. Meera, Smile Studio opened 1.3 km away on 8 Apr, undercutting your cleaning price at ₹199. I can draft a Google post emphasizing your clinical approach to differentiate you from their price-led offer. Reply YES.
rationale: I used the 'social proof' signal (the 5 positive reviews) to counter the 'loss aversion' signal (the competitor's lower price), positioning the doctor's clinical reputation as a superior differentiator. [New competitor: loss-aversion with a differentiation play grounded in the merchant's own reviews/offer.]

body: Suresh, a new restaurant just opened nearby. Your 42% repeat customer rate is your biggest strength, so let's focus on that instead of a price war. I can draft a Google post highlighting your loyal community to keep them coming back. Reply YES.
